Imagine a young person named Alex who spends a lot of time in an immersive VR game where the most popular characters engage in behaviors that, in real life, would be considered bullying, cheating, and other forms of misconduct. The game portrays these actions as cool and attractive, giving Alex the impression that such behaviors are "the in thing" to do. Over time, Alex might start to mimic these behaviors in real life, thinking they are gaining social status or fitting in, much like how someone might feel compelled to follow a wanted poster’s "cool" behaviors.
